subject: aeon
title: One Claude-Code-shaped headless contract over nine rival coding-agent CLIs
one_why: run-harness normalizes flags, stdout envelope {result,usage,session_id,cost}, exit codes, MCP config, and structured output across claude/codex/grok/kimi/pi/vibe/fx/cursor/hermes; the per-adapter rh-meta blocks generate a machine-readable capability manifest explicitly modeled on a harness-discovery protocol - no other subject treats rival CLIs as interchangeable backends with a tested contract.

subject: aeon
title: Dispatcher applies its own bwrap sandbox around whatever harness runs, because no harness enforces read-only reliably
one_why: Inverts the corpus-wide sandbox-delegation anti-pattern: measured evidence that grok's --sandbox is silently ignored, kimi/vibe/pi ship none, and claude's --allowedTools is bypassed by shell redirection, so the wrapper ro-binds the workspace (memory/ + output/ re-bound rw) uniformly; CI installs bwrap, fixes the AppArmor userns block, and self-tests the sandbox before the agent starts.

subject: aeon
title: Per-skill requires: secrets resolved from an allowlisted blob that is unset before the agent starts
one_why: Only secrets declared in a skill's frontmatter reach its env; the ALL_SECRETS blob is unset before any agent code runs; notify channel tokens were removed from the run env entirely (./notify is a queue writer, delivery is post-run); ./secretcurl keeps credentials off the agent's command line - a graduated trust model per credential blast-radius rather than one token for everything.

subject: aeon
title: Content-addressed skill lockfile (eyebrow) gating post-admission capability drift, incl. egress host sets
one_why: Targets the skill supply-chain rug pull: skills.lock pins provenance but never content, so an admitted skill that later gains an exfil endpoint passes every existing check; eyebrowlock fingerprints each SKILL.md hash AND the declared egress hosts, and CI fails only on escalation-class drift rather than every edit.

subject: aeon
title: Scheduling as the whole architecture: debt-ledger cron catch-up designed around GitHub delivering ~10% of ticks
one_why: Converges with cline's scheduled-agent-runs but pushes further: last-dispatch is treated as a debt ledger so missed slots fire once within a CATCHUP_HOURS window that doubles as max-lateness (a daily slot can never double-fire), plus an external cron-tick pinger hook - the honest way to build on a scheduler the platform under-delivers.

subject: aeon
title: Auto-recovering circuit breaker (closed/open/half-open probe) as the single source of the dispatch decision
one_why: A skill failing N consecutive times is an outage, not a flake: the breaker trades a run-per-tick burn for one probe per cooldown, resets on probe success, and lives in one tested script the scheduler calls rather than inline copies - directly portable to any long-lived agent runner loop.

subject: aeon
title: Signed run manifests via GitHub artifact attestation, with proof re-runs against a PR's attested head
one_why: Extends gptme's model-provenance-attestation into a full signed chain: a run-scoped immutable snapshot plus manifest {skill, model, mode, trigger, commit, sha256} attested with pinned attest-build-provenance, a tiered opt-in gate, and dev-loop proof runs that must not move the attested head - convergent evidence attestation is becoming a corpus theme.

subject: aeon
title: The core loop is a 2,231-line YAML workflow with a ~500-line inline Run step that nothing unit-tests
one_why: Same shape as crush/prime-agent's fused loop+policy+wiring file, in GitHub Actions YAML: the repo's own discipline extracts logic into tested scripts precisely because the inline step is untestable, but the extraction is partial - model/harness precedence, MCP gating, and the gateway cascade still live only in the workflow, where CI can't reach them.

subject: aeon
title: Three-layer read-only enforcement is opt-in: default tier is write with broad GH token and open network
one_why: Honest, documented gaps rather than hidden ones: mode:write is the default, read-only deliberately leaves egress open ('read-only is about the repo, not egress'), GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_GLOBAL stay in-run ('deferred, broad gh surface' per their own comment), and with no OS sandbox available the mode degrades to advisory with only a stderr warning.
